description: Map the Meal Gap estimates how many people lack reliable access to enough food in every US county and congressional district, and what closing that gap would cost. It is produced each year by Feeding America, the national network of food banks, using a statistical model fitted to Census Bureau and Bureau of Labor Statistics data on unemployment, poverty and household characteristics. Coverage runs from data year 2009 to 2024, with the 2026 edition published in July 2026. For each area it gives overall and child food insecurity, estimates for seniors, older adults, income bands and selected racial and ethnic groups, the share of food-insecure people above the SNAP eligibility threshold, the local cost of a meal from NielsenIQ data and the annual food budget shortfall. The data are free: the interactive map is available on the web and the full dataset is available to download after completing a request form. Caveats: figures are model estimates, not survey counts, small counties carry wide uncertainty, and methods change between editions, so years are not always comparable. Simulation uses: setting demand for food bank and emergency food distribution models, and weighting vulnerable populations in disaster food supply and evacuation planning. Related records: the USDA food security supplement (data-usda-cps-food-security-supplement) is the survey the model is calibrated to, and the USDA Food Access Research Atlas (data-usda-ers-food-access-research-atlas) maps physical access to stores.
name: Map the Meal Gap (Feeding America): annual food insecurity rates, meal costs and food budget shortfall for every US county and congressional district
schema_summary: Per county and congressional district and year: overall and child food insecurity rate and count, estimates for seniors, older adults, income bands and selected racial and ethnic groups, share above the SNAP threshold, average cost per meal and annual food budget shortfall

sources.note: Map the Meal Gap 2026 (2024 data), published 28 July 2026: food insecurity estimated for every US county and congressional district from Census Bureau and Bureau of Labor Statistics data on unemployment, poverty and household characteristics; estimates for children, seniors, older adults, income levels and races and ethnicities; cost of a meal from NielsenIQ data; national shortfall above $33 billion; average meal cost $3.70, county range $2.56 to $6.28; reports back to 2011 (2009 data)
Dataset request form: the Map the Meal Gap dataset is provided through a request form; interactive map and methodology briefs linked
